Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (FinLedger - Head of ML), Elena Gomez (FinLedger - Platform Engineer), Mark Davis (FinLedger - Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress: VPC peering, IAM/KMS access, initial benchmark results and tuning. Agreed next steps to share security docs, run a dedicated benchmark window, and finalize pricing for dedicated capacity.
topics: Security & compliance questions (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, this is our weekly POC sync. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Samir: Samir here.
[00:09] Elena: Elena on the line.
[00:11] Mark: Mark here.
[00:13] Priya: Priya from Redwood, good to see you all.
[00:15] Jordan: Cool. Agenda — quick status check on access and env readiness, review the mini-benchmark we ran last week, tuning notes, and decide on the benchmark window for dedicated runs.
[00:26] Samir: Sounds good. On access, Elena started the VPC peering request, should be in the cloud team queue, but we haven't got a CIDR back yet. IAM role is partially configured, still need the S3 test bucket access.
[00:39] Elena: yeah, I put the ticket in. We hit a little snag with our org's firewall rules; will need the exact peer IP range from you.
[00:47] Jordan: Got it, we'll share the peering ranges and a short runbook for the firewall rules. Priya, can you confirm the IP ranges?
[00:53] Priya: Yep, I'll paste the recommended range and the security group rules in the pack. Expect them in the pack Jordan sends.
[01:00] Mark: From security side, quick question — do you support customer-managed KMS, and will audit logs show individual API token usage?
[01:08] Jordan: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private / Dedicated setups; audit logs show request-level metadata, though field names in the exported logs might look different. We'll include a sample.
[01:18] Samir: Great, that's important. Also curious about data retention defaults — we want minimal retention for logs.
[01:24] Jordan: We can surface the retention controls — we'll include the defaults and how to configure them in the security pack.
[01:31] Priya: On the bench results — we ran a small workload against the hosted endpoint using your prompt set. Key numbers: steady-state throughput at ~320 tokens/sec with burst to 450, p95 latency was ~120ms for 32-token completions, p99 around 310ms.
[01:46] Samir: That p95 is a bit higher than we hoped, our target is 80-100ms at p95 for the customer-facing path.
[01:52] Priya: Understood — the test used the default batching and no quantization. A couple tuning levers we recommend: reduce batch wait to lower tail latency, enable int8 quantization for the model variant if acceptable for quality, and enable prefix KV cache for repeated contexts.
[02:06] Elena: What's the tradeoff on cost for those changes? Quantization helps but do we see any regression on correctness?
[02:12] Priya: Quantization (int8) typically reduces GPU memory and improves throughput; quality impact is model-dependent, usually minor for classification/short generation, but we should run eval prompts. We can provide a split A/B to measure. Cost-wise quantization can reduce instance size or increase throughput per GPU so lower $/token.
[02:27] Samir: For the KV cache — you mean the prefix caching? We saw notes about K-V cash in the doc (laughs) — is that safe for multi-tenant hosted?
[02:36] Jordan: Ha, yeah auto-transcription sometimes writes K-V cash. For hosted multi-tenant the cache is per-tenant and encrypted; for Dedicated/Private you have full control. We'll clarify that in the doc.
[02:46] Mark: On compliance, Samir asked about SOC2 and ISO. Do you have a SOC2 report we can send to our audit team?
[02:52] Jordan: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO certs — we'll attach PDFs in the security pack. Also include the network topology diagram and KMS policy examples.
[03:00] Elena: Good. Ok, on the environment side, timeline wise — if we get the CIDR and IAM role this week, peering could be provisioned early next week. Then we can open the benchmark window.
[03:11] Priya: For the benchmark, we recommend a 2-hour window with production-like traffic and the dev prompt set Samir will provide. We'll instrument RPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and token cost.
[03:21] Samir: We'll curate a 2000-prompt sample, weighted by our query distribution, and share it by Friday.
[03:26] Jordan: Great. On pricing — you asked for an estimate for Dedicated capacity. I put together a draft based on expected QPS; I'll share the draft and we can iterate.
[03:36] Samir: Are there any minimum commitments?
[03:38] Jordan: For Dedicated we generally do a monthly reserved capacity with a 3-month minimum in pilot phases, but flexible options exist for ramp. We'll mark that in the pricing email.
[03:46] Elena: One technical thing — our infra team noticed connector config for S3 expects a role ARN with sts:AssumeRole. Is there a sample policy?
[03:55] Priya: Yes, sample role JSON and bucket policy will be in the runbook. Also note we can accept token-based uploads if that's simpler.
[04:03] Mark: Any concerns about data residency? We need EU-only processing for some datasets.
[04:08] Jordan: We have region pins for model routing; for your EU data we can route to the EU region endpoints and document the flow. For Private deployments we can keep everything on-prem.
[04:17] Samir: One more on the bench: the initial run used batch sizes set to 8. If we lower to 2 or 4, will that meaningfully change p95?
[04:24] Priya: Lower batch size reduces latency at the cost of throughput. For your latency goals I'd suggest dynamic batching with a low max batch (4) and a small microbatch wait (2-5ms). We'll test that in the benchmark.
[04:34] Elena: Also curious about memory use. The model we tested was the 7B variant; do you see a reason to move to quantized 13B instead?
[04:41] Priya: 13B quantized can sometimes match 7B float performance on certain tasks but it's model-dependent. We'll include a quick eval comparing 7B float, 7B int8, and 13B int8 in the benchmark plan.
[04:52] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps. Jordan to send security pack and draft pricing. Priya to prep benchmark scripts and runbook. Elena to provision IAM and S3 tests and finalize VPC CIDR. Samir to provide prompt set. Mark to confirm KMS policy constraints.
[05:05] Samir: Sounds good. Anything else on questions?
[05:08] Mark: Could you also include an example of the audit log exports (format) so our compliance team can parse it?
[05:14] Jordan: Yes, sample logs included.
[05:16] Elena: Are we scheduling the benchmark now or after peering?
[05:19] Priya: After peering and IAM are verified; we'll propose windows for the week of 2026-03-30.
[05:24] Jordan: I'll send the calendar poll after this call. Thanks everyone.
[05:27] Samir: Thanks all.
[05:28] Mark: Thanks.
[05:29] Priya: Bye.
[05:30] Jordan: End call.

Notes: transcription contains minor errors ("K-V cash" etc). Bench numbers are preliminary; final benchmark to be run in dedicated window.
